key_insight: Evaluator-guided LLM search discovers quantum circuits that reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts in seven of eight tasks and a new modular-inversion architecture in the eighth.
engineering_relevance: More resource-efficient reversible primitives could lower quantum-computing costs across numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, simulation, and number theory.
method: Use LLMs to propose circuit designs in an evolutionary search.
Independently verify and score candidate circuits.
Explore new reversible architectures alongside circuit optimizations.
evidence_signal: Across eight tasks, the abstract reports significant Toffoli and qubit reductions in seven and an improved Toffoli–qubit trade-off for prime-field modular inversion using divsteps in the eighth.
watch_item: Circuit resource reductions do not establish hardware-level speedups; the abstract does not report physical-device validation.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
